Language switch

.dr-lang · button[aria-pressed] · components/lang.css · kit specimen

Anatomy

  1. 1.dr-langThe container: 32 high, radius 12, no border. Two flush halves read as one control with two states, not as two buttons that touch.
  2. 2button[aria-pressed="true"]The chosen language: Signal Green behind charcoal, 9.46:1, plus the --shadow-sm the primary button wears.
  3. 3button[aria-pressed="false"]The other: --btn2 behind --ink, 11.54:1, no shadow. Hover steps to --media.

Variants and sizes

Inventory rows: Language switch.

When to use

The language switch sets the interface language, English (primary) or Ukrainian. It is the shell's control: the wireframe shell injects it into the top bar opposite the brand, and it shows only in the desktop preview. The mobile nav bar carries the back control and one name, so a second control on its right is a desktop question. .dr-lang is the component that injection expresses, and no product page draws it directly. It is coloured as the buttons are, primary and secondary, which makes it a second green control on the screens it stands on, about 0.3% of the frame. That is recorded rather than argued.

The labels are the two-letter codes, EN and UA. The group is named Language.

Sources: wireframes/_wf-shell.js § Language switch · inventory.md § 1.5 · DESIGN.md § Elevation & Depth (pressed language toggle) · CLAUDE.md § Interface Languages

Rule and anti-rule

Do

The desktop top bar: the switch at the trailing edge, opposite the brand, available from every screen.

Don’t

This block shows the right control for the phone, where the switch does not go. On mobile, language is a setting on account-edit: a picker row that opens a two-option drawer. Do not put the switch in the mobile nav bar, and do not use it for other two-way choices. A value in a form is a radio, and a setting that applies on the tap is a switch.
